claims.nodeLabel: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report
claims.text: AARO's HRR Volume I lists the 'UAP Independent Study Team (UAPIST) (June 2022-September 2023)' as one of the official USG UAP investigatory efforts it reviewed (Table of Contents, Section IV, p. 25).

NEGATIVE PRIMARY FINDING: a full-text search of the released AARO Historical Record Report Volume I (63 pp., DOPSR-cleared 6 Mar 2024) returns zero hits for 'Yankee', 'Kirtland', 'AFOSI', 'Office of Special Investigations', 'initiation' and 'hazing'. Yankee Blue is NOT documented in HRR Volume I. Any citation of Volume I as the source for the Yankee Blue / Kirtland-AFOSI account is incorrect.

The only named sensitive programs disclosed in HRR Volume I's Section VI ('Investigation into Named USG Sensitive Programs', pp. 33-36) are KONA BLUE, the Virtual Institute for Satellite Integration Training, and an unnamed IC Controlled Access Program 'unnecessarily expanded in 2021 to include a UAP reverse-engineering mission'. Yankee Blue is not among them.

Yankee Blue therefore has no Tier 1 anchor in the AARO documentary record as of 12 Aug 2026. The public account rests on June 2025 press reporting and on statements attributed to AARO officials describing an Air Force hazing/indoctrination practice at Kirtland AFB in which personnel were falsely read into a non-existent UAP program; the underlying memo has not been released. Reasoning: direct full-text verification against the only AARO report that could plausibly have contained it, plus the absence of any Yankee Blue reference in the FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports (also searched, zero hits).

b.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)

edges.note: The report is where the Department's own account of AATIP sits. Volume I records that AAWSAP 'was also known [as] AATIP' and that DIA cancelled the programme in 2012, then that supporters proposed KONA BLUE to DHS as a follow-on. That is the programmatic relation: the report covers the programme's lifecycle. The denial edge on this pair is separate and records the report's rejection of the reverse-engineering account.

a.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I

edges.note: The report is the object of the search, which is what makes this investigative rather than a denial. A full-text pass of Volume I returns no occurrence of 'Yankee Blue' across all 63 pages including endnotes 1-200. That negative finding is what refuted the widely repeated claim - asserted on this board until 12 August 2026 - that AARO conceded the programme in Volume I.

b.label: AARO Historical Record Report, Volume II (unpublished)

edges.note: AARO is the office that OWES this volume, which is a different relationship from having withheld it. Sec. 6802 places the duty on the Director of the Office, and Volume I commits to it twice in its own text: page 6, 'AARO will publish Volume II in accordance with the date established in Section 6802', and page 45, 'This report represents Volume I of AARO's HR2.' The denial edge on this same pair records the non-delivery; this one records whose obligation it is.

edges.note: AARO's official history states: 'At the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats to the United States.' It further records that on 24 June 2009 Reid wrote to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III asking that the programme be made a Special Access Program. Tier 2: AARO is an interested party in its own institutional history.
